name: CoLearn (colearn.id; Indonesian app 'CoLearn: Aplikasi MTK, fisika', plus the newer English-language spin-off 'CoLearn Tutor' / 'CoTutor' by IQ Edu Pte Ltd)
origin_region: Indonesia — founded 2019 in Jakarta by Abhay Saboo (CEO) and Marc Irawan; corporate entity IQ Edu Pte Ltd (Singapore-registered), Android package com.iq.colearn. Raised ~USD 27-34M total, including a USD 10M Series A (April 2021) led by Alpha Wave Incubation and GSV Ventures and a USD 17M extension. A newer companion product, CoLearn Tutor / CoTutor (com.iqedu.colearntutor), launched 9 January 2025 in English and appears aimed at a wider/Indian market — its version history references JEE preparation
target_age: Indonesian app: grade 5 of elementary school through grade 12 of senior high school (ages ~10-18). The Play Store description states 'an online Bimbel app for Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry from 5th grade of elementary school to 12th grade of high school'; the Tanya video library is labelled for SD grades 5-6, SMP and SMA. Critically, grades 1-4 SD are NOT served. The colearn.id site frames coverage as grade 4 SD upward with heavy emphasis on exam cohorts (TKA, PAS/PAT, SNBT) [uncertain — site copy and app copy differ on whether the floor is grade 4 or grade 5]. The English CoTutor app is rated 9+ / 'Rated for 3+' and claims grades 3-12
delivery_mode: hybrid within a single app — the current centre of gravity is scheduled LIVE online group tutoring (online bimbel), not self-serve homework help. Play Store tagline as of August 2026: 'CoLearn: Online bimbel app, 2 classes per week'. Students pick a schedule, join 60-minute live classes with a consistent peer cohort and a 'Guru Juara' teacher across a semester, then download PDF and video recap material. Alongside this sits Tanya, an on-demand searchable library of 300,000+ pre-recorded solution videos, and weekly non-multiple-choice exercises that require handwritten working. The original 'snap a photo of the problem' framing has been de-emphasised relative to its 2020-2021 press coverage
language_localization: Fully native Bahasa Indonesia and Indonesian-built — UI, teacher instruction, 300,000+ solution videos, and parent communication are all in Indonesian, produced domestically. Parent reports are pushed in Indonesian over WhatsApp, the dominant local channel. This is among the strongest localizations in the competitor set. Note the divergence: the newer CoTutor spin-off is English-only, so its more advanced work-analysis capability is NOT available to an Indonesian-speaking child
pricing_model: freemium plus subscription. The app is free to download with in-app purchases; the Tanya solution-video library is the free/low-friction hook. Paid live tutoring (bimbel) is a monthly subscription: approximately Rp 90,000/month for mathematics once a week, Rp 170,000/month for twice a week, +Rp 80,000/month to add science, and Rp 170,000/month for a grade-12 intensive track of four classes a week (2026/2027 pricing), with a 100% first-month money-back guarantee. The English CoTutor uses a consumable 'energy' credit model instead: 30 free energies granted on the 1st of each month, with 30 more for USD 0.99
local_curriculum_alignment: Yes, explicit. Indonesian press and CoLearn's own package descriptions state that CoLearn material follows the government curriculum, Kurikulum Merdeka, and packages bundle 'Kelas Live + Latihan Mingguan + Laporan Belajar'. Product framing is organised around Indonesian assessment milestones — PAS/PAT, TKA, and SNBT university entrance — which is genuine local alignment but also anchors the product to exam-oriented secondary schooling rather than foundational primary numeracy
does_error_type_diagnosis: no for the Indonesian product; partial and unvalidated for the English-only CoTutor spin-off. The Indonesian CoLearn app's core loop is answer-delivery: search or photograph a question, receive an expert-verified video walking through the correct solution. That is a worked-example service — it explains how the problem SHOULD be solved and never inspects what the child actually wrote, so it cannot distinguish a misreading from a concept error from an arithmetic slip. The one Indonesian mechanism that touches student work is the weekly non-multiple-choice exercise requiring handwritten working, which is reviewed by a human teacher inside the live-class relationship rather than by an error-classification engine, and the resulting parent report surfaces attendance and exam readiness, not error categories. The separate English CoTutor product does move closer: it withholds the answer until the student writes their attempt, then 'AI analyzes their work, identifies mistakes'. But 'identifies mistakes' is mistake-spotting on a single attempt, not classification into a named taxonomy of error kinds, and no taxonomy or category list is published anywhere
diagnosis_granularity: Indonesian app: score-only / trouble-spot-quantity at best — the parent-facing report covers attendance, weekly exercise completion, and a coarse exam-readiness signal; the Tanya library has no per-student model at all. English CoTutor: unlabelled mistake-spotting on the student's own written attempt, which sits between trouble-spot-quantity and a true error-type taxonomy but stops short of the latter because no error categories are named or reported. Neither product ships a distractor-mapped misconception model or a full error-type taxonomy
diagnosis_input_modality: Indonesian app: photo/OCR and text search of the QUESTION, not of the student's work — students either type a problem description into a search field or photograph the problem, and the system retrieves a matching pre-made solution video. This is retrieval, not diagnosis: the input carries no information about the child's own reasoning. Weekly exercises are free-response and handwritten but are collected for a human teacher. English CoTutor: photo of the student's own handwritten attempt (free-response OCR of student working), with output delivered as audio rather than text, deliberately, 'to keep students focused on their own notebook instead of a screen'. No handwriting-stroke capture in either product
ai_tutor_diagnosis_reliability: Unvalidated in both products, and the reliable-diagnosis claim is weakest exactly where it matters. No ground-truth validation study, accuracy benchmark, or documented failure-mode disclosure exists for CoLearn's or CoTutor's mistake identification. The Indonesian product is architecturally immune to the question because it never diagnoses — but that same architecture is the textbook 'correct answer trap': a child who arrives at the right answer by an unsound method, or who copies the video's method without understanding, is indistinguishable to the system from one who genuinely understands, and Indonesian press coverage from launch onward praised precisely the speed of getting a worked answer. CoTutor's design partially mitigates this by gating the answer behind a written attempt ('No effort = No answers'), which forces the child to externalise reasoning before help arrives — a sound anti-copying mechanism — but its analysis quality is unmeasured, and its market signal is weak: 10K+ Play Store installs and a 2.0/5 App Store rating from a single rating as of August 2026. Treat any diagnosis claim as vendor marketing [uncertain]
evidence_quote: CoTutor / CoLearn Tutor Play Store description (com.iqedu.colearntutor, updated 30 July 2026): 'CoLearn Tutor is the AI tutor that helps students think—not just copy answers. • Students must first attempt math and science problems by writing what they know. • AI analyzes their work, identifies mistakes, and provides personalized audio guidance. • No effort = No answers. Students can't get solutions without first trying. … • Parents can track their child's learning journey and see genuine effort.' The marketing site colearntutor.com adds 'CoLearn evaluates your work and spots errors' — note 'spots errors', with no error categories named. Decisively on the parent/child channel question, the same site states: 'Your child cannot have conversations with us. Interactions are limited to analyzing their questions and their work' and 'CoLearn is built for children, but it works best with encouragement from parents.' By contrast the Indonesian app description (com.iq.colearn, updated 11 August 2026) contains no diagnosis language at all: 'CoLearn is an online Bimbel app for Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry from 5th grade of elementary school to 12th grade of high school … Study online in classes with expert Guru Juara and Mentor graduated from the best universities.' On the Indonesian Tanya feature: '300,000+ video pembahasan soal' and 'Semua video udah dicek kebenarannya' (all videos have been verified for accuracy)
how_parent_involved: gatekeeper plus push-report dashboard — one of the stronger parent postures in the Indonesian set, but informational rather than diagnostic. The parent is the payer for the monthly bimbel subscription, so they are a genuine purchase gatekeeper, and CoLearn pushes reports to them proactively: colearn.id advertises progress reporting 'Langsung ke WhatsApp orang tua' (straight to the parent's WhatsApp), covering attendance and exam-readiness monitoring, and Indonesian press coverage notes 'Orang tua juga bisa mendapatkan laporan rutin terhadap hasil belajar anak' (parents can also receive regular reports on their child's learning results). Packages bundle a 'Laporan Belajar' as a named deliverable. What the parent receives is attendance, completion and score/readiness signals — not an explanation of what kind of mistake their child keeps making, and not a script for how to help. In the English CoTutor the parent role is narrower still and framed around effort verification: parents 'track their child's learning journey and see genuine effort', i.e. proof the child wrote something rather than copied, plus the explicit instruction that the product 'works best with encouragement from parents'
ai_tutor_directly_to_child: no in the Indonesian product; deliberately one-way and non-conversational in the English spin-off. The Indonesian CoLearn app puts a HUMAN in front of the child — live 60-minute classes with a Guru Juara teacher and mentors — supplemented by pre-recorded, human-made solution videos; there is no AI chat companion. CoTutor does put an AI directly in front of the child without a parent intermediary, but it is explicitly not a chatbot: the product states 'Your child cannot have conversations with us. Interactions are limited to analyzing their questions and their work', and guidance is delivered as one-way personalized audio while the child looks at their own notebook. This is a notable and deliberate product stance — CoLearn's team appears to have concluded that open-ended AI conversation with a child is a risk to be designed out, choosing gated, work-anchored audio feedback instead
key_finding: CoLearn is Indonesia's most-installed homework-help brand, but it has repositioned away from the very thing the market gap concerns, and its most diagnosis-like capability is locked behind the wrong language and the wrong market. Three findings matter. (1) The Indonesian flagship no longer leads with photo-a-problem homework help — as of August 2026 its Play Store identity is 'Online bimbel app, 2 classes per week', i.e. subscription live group tutoring, with the 300,000-video Tanya library demoted to a support feature. Its diagnosis remains zero: Tanya matches a photographed or typed QUESTION to a pre-made correct-solution video and never reads the child's work, so it is a worked-example retrieval engine, and the only inspection of actual student working is a human teacher reviewing weekly handwritten exercises. (2) The company clearly recognises the error-diagnosis gap and built for it — CoTutor withholds answers until the child writes an attempt, then analyses that written work to identify mistakes — but it shipped that product in ENGLISH only, aimed at a different market (JEE references), with just 10K+ installs and a 2.0/5 rating, while the 5M-download Indonesian app got none of it. Even there, 'identifies mistakes' is unlabelled mistake-spotting; no error-type taxonomy is published. (3) Parent involvement is real but shallow: WhatsApp-pushed reports on attendance and exam readiness make the parent an informed payer, not an equipped coach — they learn THAT the child is behind, never WHAT KIND of mistake is recurring or what to do about it. Two coverage gaps compound this: the floor is grade 5 SD (grades 1-4 unserved), and both products are anchored to exam-prep for secondary cohorts. Also note two corrections to the working brief — CoLearn is now 5M+ Play Store downloads at 4.4/5 from 39.5K reviews, not 1M+ at 4.5, and its dominant business model is paid live tutoring rather than free homework help
study_scale_or_sample: Market/adoption figures rather than research samples, captured 15 August 2026. Indonesian app (com.iq.colearn): 5M+ Play Store downloads, 4.4 stars from 39.5K reviews, last updated 11 August 2026, Education category, in-app purchases, 2020 Google Play Best Personal Growth App winner. Content scale: 300,000+ verified solution videos across Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry. colearn.id claims 10,000+ currently enrolled live-class students across Indonesia. Funding: USD 10M Series A (April 2021, Alpha Wave Incubation and GSV Ventures) plus a USD 17M extension, ~USD 27-34M total. English CoTutor (com.iqedu.colearntutor): 10K+ Play Store installs, updated 30 July 2026, released 9 January 2025, rebranded to CoTutor 28 July 2025, 2.0/5 App Store rating from 1 rating. Note the two-order-of-magnitude gap between the Indonesian install base and the work-analysis product's install base
evidence_strength: moderate. Distribution and rating figures were read directly from the live Google Play and App Store listings and are strong. Feature claims come from CoLearn's own first-party marketing surfaces (colearn.id, colearntutor.com, store descriptions), which is strong evidence of what is claimed but weak evidence of what actually works — none of it is independently tested. The key negative finding, that the Indonesian product does no error-type diagnosis, rests on the absence of any such claim across the app description, the Tanya feature page and the pricing pages, plus the positive presence of a retrieval-based mechanism that structurally cannot diagnose; that is a well-supported inference but still partly argument-from-silence. The exact SD grade floor is inconsistent between CoLearn's own site and its app listing. No independent product teardown or user study of CoLearn's diagnosis quality was found
remediation_efficacy_evidence: None found. There is no RCT, quasi-experimental study, or independent evaluation showing that CoLearn's reports, its solution videos, or CoTutor's mistake identification improve learning outcomes. Evidence offered by the company is commercial and testimonial: download counts, star ratings, funding rounds, a 100% first-month money-back guarantee, and claims that solution videos are 'expert-verified' for correctness — verification of the CONTENT's accuracy, which is not evidence of the child's LEARNING. The most rigorous-sounding mechanism, CoTutor's attempt-before-answer gate, is a plausible anti-copying design with no published outcome data behind it. Indonesian academic literature on CoLearn specifically was not located; the 2020-2021 coverage in CNN Indonesia, Kompas, Kontan and Detik is product-launch journalism rather than evaluation
